Bitstream autopsy: which FPGA a 7-series .bit really targets

Drop a Xilinx 7-series .bit: header, the IDCODE it writes and the part that names, frames, zero bytes and packets, read in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

A file you open here is read by your browser only: it is never uploaded. The page sets no cookie and sends nothing anywhere.

Where the numbers come from
  • gHashTag/t27 commit c129a5b9e9f0: fpga/openxc7-synth/blink_j26.bit, find_led.bit, static_d5.bit, test_top.bit and phi_temporal/temporal_heartbeat.bit (read with git show; t27#6222)
  • build-receipt widget bitstream build_receipt.bit for xc7a200tfbg676-1, sha256 f1da88bc8f4660ff3e68dd050ae9277553a59897739f7a5b0b768fc7868e25a6
  • prjxray bitread commit c9f02d85 (2025-06-05): bitread -part_file prjxray-db/artix7/<part>/part.yaml -z -o and -x -z -o; frame, non-zero frame and set-bit counts equal ours for all six samples
  • openFPGALoader v1.1.1 (85be4fa0) src/part.hpp via the idcode widget's parts.json, checked against prjxray-db ab1fc60 artix7 part.json (rows, columns, IDCODEs)
  • AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration: bitstream header, sync word, packet types, registers, commands, IDCODE check and ID_ERROR
